Posterior predictive checks for mvgam models

Source: R/pp_check.mvgam.R
pp_check.mvgam.Rd

Compares the observed response with replicates drawn from the fitted model through the bayesplot ppc_* functions. Further types plot randomised quantile residuals and, for nmix() and occ() fits, a discrepancy statistic. Returns a ggplot2 object.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
pp_check(
  object,
  type,
  ndraws = NULL,
  prefix = c("ppc", "ppd"),
  group = NULL,
  x = NULL,
  newdata = NULL,
  resp = NULL,
  draw_ids = NULL,
  per_obs = TRUE,
  series = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An object of class mvgam

type

Type of the check. A bayesplot ppc_* or ppd_* function named without its prefix, or one of the residual types mvgam adds: "resid_hist", "resid_hist_grouped", "resid_ribbon", "resid_ribbon_grouped", "resid_qq", "resid_vs_fitted", "resid_acf", "resid_pacf" and "resid_variogram". Type "fit_stat" serves nmix() and occ() fits. A bernoulli or ordinal response defaults to "bars". Another discrete response, such as a count, defaults to "rootogram". A continuous response defaults to "dens_overlay". Multi-response families take the defaults under "Multi-response families".

ndraws

Number of posterior draws to plot. NULL (the default) takes the default of the type, listed under Details.

prefix

"ppc" (the default) plots the observed data with the replicates. "ppd" plots the replicates alone.

group

Optional name of a factor variable in the model by which to stratify the ppc plot. This argument is required for ppc *_grouped types and ignored otherwise.

x

Optional name of a variable in the model. Only used for ppc types having an x argument and ignored otherwise.

newdata

Optional data frame of the variables in the model. NULL (the default) checks the training data. The residual types describe the training data and refuse newdata.

resp

Optional names of response variables. If specified, predictions are performed only for the specified response variables.

draw_ids

Optional integer vector naming the posterior draws to plot. NULL (the default) lets ndraws choose them.

per_obs

Logical. For type = "resid_vs_fitted", TRUE (the default) draws each observation at its posterior median on both axes. FALSE draws every draw of every observation, which shows the posterior spread.

series

For the residual types resid_hist, resid_ribbon, resid_qq, resid_vs_fitted, resid_acf, resid_pacf and resid_variogram, the one series whose residuals are drawn, as a name or an index. The default is the first series. Its residuals are taken in time order. resid_acf keeps missing responses in place. Its lags count time steps. resid_pacf drops them. Its lags count observations. A fit with several series names its series in the subtitle.

...

Further arguments of posterior_predict.mvgam() and of the bayesplot function type names. Any other name is refused. type = "fit_stat" takes stat, either "chi_squared" (the default) or "freeman_tukey".

Value

A ggplot object. A multivariate model given no resp returns one figure with a panel per response. type = "fit_stat" returns an mvgam_ppc_fit_stat object with print and plot methods.

Details

Replicates of the training data are drawn under the latent trend state the model inferred at each time, as residuals.mvgam() and hindcast.mvgam() use. The check then compares the fitted trajectory with the series that produced it. Replicates of newdata use the covariate part of the model, as posterior_predict.mvgam() does. Passing incl_autocor chooses between the two. The loo_* types use the fitted state. Their importance weights come from it.

Overlay types default to 10 draws. Interval, ribbon and statistic types use every draw. The residual histograms and ribbons default to 500 draws, the other residual types to 100 and fit_stat to 500. A posterior with fewer draws gives all of them. resid_hist draws one histogram per draw and shows the first eight.

resid_acf and resid_pacf count lags in rows. They refuse a series observed at unevenly spaced times, such as one a CAR() trend models. resid_variogram measures lags in time units. It plots half the mean squared difference of two residuals against the time between them. Residuals without serial dependence give a flat semivariogram at their variance, the dashed line (Diggle et al. 2002). plot(type = "residuals") draws it in place of the ACF and pACF for such a series.

The PPC documentation of bayesplot describes each ppc_* type. A check restricted to one series or covariate slice takes newdata filtered to those rows. The _grouped types take group = "series" to draw one panel per series.

Multi-response families

diri(), multi(), categ(), mvn() and mvt() record several outcomes per unit. A pooled density would merge them into one curve. Without a group from the caller, pp_check() draws one panel per species through the type's _grouped variant. The default type is "ribbon" for a composition and "dens_overlay" for mvn() and mvt(). Passing a column of newdata as group draws the pooled plot.

Detection families (nmix(), occ())

The visits of a closure unit share one latent state. pp_check() sums the observed and replicated visits of each unit and compares the sums. The count types (bars, rootogram, hist, freqpoly), the density and ECDF overlays, the statistic types, intervals, ribbon, resid_hist and resid_qq apply. Types that plot rows, residuals against fitted values or residuals over time are refused. A group or x column must be constant within each unit. type = "fit_stat" computes the chi-squared or Freeman-Tukey discrepancy of Gelman et al. (1996) from the unit sums.

References

Diggle, P. J., Heagerty, P., Liang, K.-Y. and Zeger, S. L. (2002). Analysis of Longitudinal Data, 2nd edition. Oxford University Press.

Gabry, J., Simpson, D., Vehtari, A., Betancourt, M. and Gelman, A. (2019). Visualization in Bayesian workflow. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society A, 182:389-402. doi:10.1111/rssa.12378

Gelman, A., Meng, X.-L. and Stern, H. (1996). Posterior predictive assessment of model fitness via realized discrepancies. Statistica Sinica, 6:733-760.

See also

residuals.mvgam() returns the residuals the residual types plot. CAR() models series observed at unevenly spaced times. loo.mvgam() scores the fit. The overview article explains a rootogram. The N-mixture article runs the discrepancy check.

Other model checking: mvgam_diagnostics, plot.mvgam(), residuals.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
             data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
             chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 5 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# A hanging rootogram, on the square-root scale. Each bar shows how
# often a count was observed. It hangs from the curve of its expected
# frequency under the model. A bar ending below zero marks a count the
# model under-predicts
pp_check(mod, type = "rootogram", style = "hanging")


# Randomised quantile residuals over time. A trend the model missed
# shows as serial structure
pp_check(mod, type = "resid_ribbon")


# Half the mean squared difference of residuals by the time between
# them. A flat band at the dashed variance shows no dependence left
pp_check(mod, type = "resid_variogram")


# Next: plot(mod, type = "residuals") shows the residual grid
# }
